title: Spin-sensitive constructions attaining the maximal disjoint-cylinder count in every holomorphic Abelian component
difficulty_reason: H2: the known bound g+n-1 and existence in some stratum component do not force attainment in each hyperelliptic or spin-parity component. The author gives explicit polar-domain gluing orders, handles the genus3 hyperelliptic/odd cases and higher-genus hyperelliptic/two-spin cases separately, and computes the homology-loop indices needed to distinguish the spin parities. A stable degeneration and zero splitting then adds one cylinder per extra zero while staying in the required component. The new direct component-sensitive gluing and spin calculation carry the burden; Naveh upper bound and the stable-cylinder equivalence/circumference applications are named inputs or uncounted consequences.

editorial_notes: Retain original author statements/proofs and all inline TikZ illustrations unchanged; author mathematics is not independently certified, corrected or supplemented.
Types have strictly positive zero orders, higher pole orders b_j>=2 and s simple poles. Preserve the partition sum 2g-2 and the exclusion of the empty one-simple-pole strata.
Residual space is C^p times (C*)^s with total sum zero: residues at higher order poles may vanish, simple-pole residues cannot.
Author residue convention is 2*pi*i times the usual analytic residue; retain it for gluing, flat periods and cylinder statements.
Primitive integral signed residue data use the collective gcd of all positive integers equal to1 and a common nonzero complex scaling factor, not pairwise coprimality.
